newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa to ask private sector to build, run jails.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa to ask private sector to build, run jails.

text.p: Foreign and local companies will for the first time be invited to bid for the construction and operation of seven jails in South Africa, prisons minister Sipo Mzimela said on Tuesday.

He told a news conference that the tendering process would open on April 21 for the jails -- two of them super-maximum security facilities housing 1,500 inmates each -- and that construction should start on October 1.

"We know for a fact that this will contribute greatly to our fight against crime," Mzimela said, adding that South Africa's jails were holding 50 percent more prisoners than the number for which they were designed.
Overcrowding, outdated security features and corrupt wardens mean that escapes from South African jails are routine.

The super-maximum jails, which would be the first to be built in South Africa, "are designed to house very dangerous criminals who have shown by their behaviour that they cannot be part of society", Mzimela said.
Inmates would be locked in their cells for 23 hours a day with one hour for exercise.
Mzimela said South Africa was following the example of countries like the United States and Britain by involving the private sector in building and running its jails.
"The whole idea is based on the assumption that the government will never have enough money to build the kind of facilities that South Africa needs," he said.
Mzimela said the government was still studying the idea, mooted by his department earlier this year, that disused mine shafts could be converted to super-maximum security jails.
He said South Africa now spent about 70 rand ($15) a day per prisoner.
